description: Default-deny capability for the main window — no fs:, no bare shell:, only core defaults, window management, the narrow dialog:allow-open grant for the project registration folder picker (T-01-02), and a shell:allow-execute grant scoped to exactly one named sidecar binary (plan 02-01, T-02-01/T-02-09) — the renderer itself has no shell capability at all; only the Rust core's own sidecar supervisor (src-tauri/src/sidecar.rs) invokes tauri-plugin-shell, and this scoped grant is what makes that invocation the ONLY process this app's shell permission can ever launch. Tauri v2's ACL/permission system gates PLUGIN commands (dialog:*, core:*, shell:*); this app's own #[tauri::command] handlers are not plugin commands and are exposed solely via main.rs's generate_handler! list, which is the actual default-deny boundary for them — no permissions/ directory defines custom ACL entries for them in this project, so listing them here would have no runtime effect (verified empirically: project_register/project_list/task_create/board_list from plan 01-03 already work without such an entry). Full app-command roster, kept here for auditability since generate_handler! is the enforcement point: project_register, project_list, project_reconcile, project_relocate, task_create, task_update, task_delete, task_set_status, task_reorder, task_set_priority, task_set_estimate, task_set_assignee, epic_create, epic_update, epic_delete, epic_set_status, epic_reorder, epic_set_priority, epic_set_estimate, epic_set_assignee, issue_create, issue_update, issue_delete, issue_reorder, board_list, board_search, actor_list, criterion_create, criterion_update, criterion_toggle, criterion_reorder, criterion_delete, criterion_list, events_activity_trail, events_since_cursor, agent_run_preview, agent_run_start, agent_run_log_window, agent_run_raw_window, agent_runs_for_task, agent_run_acknowledge, worktree_summary, worktree_remove_check, worktree_remove, worktree_recreate, worktree_forget_record, agent_run_stop, agent_run_answer_permission, permission_rules_list, permission_rule_revoke, agent_run_pending_permissions, task_latest_agent_run, board_blocked_summary, agent_runs_pending_orphans, orphan_kill, settings_get, settings_set_credential_mode, settings_store_api_key, settings_clear_api_key, backend_capability_probe. board_search (plan 01-08, BOARD-06) is named explicitly here rather than covered by any blanket grant (T-01-02) — free-text search and every filter dimension still run as indexed, parameterised SQL inside packages/core, this command only carries the request/response across the IPC boundary. events_activity_trail/events_since_cursor (plan 01-10, BOARD-09/DATA-05) are both read-only and both cap their requested window server-side (T-01-24) before calling into packages/core. project_reconcile/project_relocate (plan 01-11, BOARD-10/D-16) never enumerate the filesystem and never write board content into a user's repository — project_reconcile re-verifies each project's already-known marker path, project_relocate writes only the identity marker at the user-chosen path after verifying it names the expected project id (T-01-29). agent_run_preview (plan 02-04, D-27/D-28) is read-only — it mutates nothing, creates no worktree and writes no trigger row, so the launch sheet costs nothing until Start Work actually fires. agent_run_start/agent_run_log_window (plan 02-01, AGNT-01/D-04) validate permission_mode against a fixed four-value list, reject an instruction over 4000 characters (plan 02-04, T-02-20), and cap the log window at 100 rows server-side before ever reaching packages/core (T-02-06); agent_run_start (plan 02-09) also resolves the run's credential exactly once per spawn (D-39) and attaches it to the child's environment only, never to argv. agent_run_raw_window (plan 02-07, D-32/T-02-06) is read-only — the raw view's own bounded read over the identical persisted log, returning each line's verbatim text rather than a parsed value, capped server-side at the same 100-row ceiling. agent_runs_for_task/worktree_summary (plan 02-07, 02-UI-SPEC.md "Runs section"/"Worktree summary") are both read-only, bounded reads feeding the item detail panel's two new sections, mutating nothing. agent_run_acknowledge (plan 03-10, D-49) is read-only in effect on everything except a single timestamp column (acknowledged_at), resolves the actor server-side, and is guarded to the abandoned status in its own SQL WHERE clause — acknowledging a non-abandoned run is a no-op and this command can never change a run's status. worktree_remove_check/worktree_remove (plan 03-01, WORK-03/D-41/D-42/D-43) are the worktree-removal surface: worktree_remove_check is a read-only, never-cached git status --porcelain read taken fresh at dialog-open time; worktree_remove resolves the actor server-side and re-reads porcelain itself inside packages/core before ever calling git worktree remove, refusing unconditionally on any uncommitted change — no parameter on this surface, at any layer, can skip that guard. worktree_recreate/worktree_forget_record (plan 03-09, WORK-06/D-45) are D-45's two missing-worktree recovery decisions: both resolve the actor server-side; worktree_recreate recreates a worktree only from the branch and base already recorded on the row and never resolves a new base ref; worktree_forget_record deletes only a database row and makes no filesystem call. agent_run_stop (plan 02-02, PROC-06/D-35) resolves the actor server-side (T-02-13), sends the sidecar's interrupt request and blocks on its ack before writing the run's terminal status, and never touches git — the worktree is left exactly as the agent left it. agent_run_answer_permission (plan 02-05, AGNT-06/D-38) rejects a decision outside allow/deny/allow_always before touching the database, resolves the actor server-side, and relays nothing to the sidecar when the target row is no longer pending. permission_rules_list is read-only; permission_rule_revoke resolves the actor server-side and appends a revocation event. agent_run_pending_permissions/task_latest_agent_run (plan 02-06, AGNT-06) are both read-only — the permission-request card's data source and the item detail panel's own resolution of a task's active run, mutating nothing. board_blocked_summary (plan 02-06, D-37) is read-only — the board's blocked-row indicator and project-rail count read, delegating straight to query::permissions. agent_runs_pending_orphans/orphan_kill (plan 03-06, PROC-05/D-46/D-48) are the launch-time orphan-recovery surface: both resolve the actor server-side (T-01-04), agent_runs_pending_orphans is read-only (it clones the launch classification's own list, populated once at startup, and never re-scans), and orphan_kill signals a process GROUP recorded by this application's own previous run — never a pid supplied by the renderer (T-03-06-03) — rejecting with a not-found error rather than a false success when the named run is no longer pending. settings_get/settings_set_credential_mode/settings_store_api_key/settings_clear_api_key/backend_capability_probe (plan 02-09, D-39) are the credential boundary's command surface — no command in this group ever returns the API key value itself (settings_get reports only whether a key is configured and the date), settings_set_credential_mode validates scope/mode against fixed vocabularies before touching the database, and backend_capability_probe is read-only (it never spawns a session and never touches a credential).
